title.narrative: Weaving a Safer Future for Older Women in Narok County

description.narrative: The Coalition on Violence Against Women (COVAW) proposes targeted interventions in Narok county aimed at mitigating and responding to Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) against older women, a group often invisible in both public discourse and service provision despite facing unique and growing vulnerabilities. In many rural areas, older women suffer in silence due to ageism, harmful social norms, stigma, and limited access to justice and support services. This project seeks to centre their voices, enhance their agency, and build a responsive ecosystem that will protect, empower, and enable them to access survivor-centred SGBV services. A vital component of the intervention will be sustained community engagement designed to challenge deep-rooted silence and cultural norms and stereotypes surrounding both SGBV and ageing. Through intergenerational dialogues and community-led forums, COVAW will challenge violence against older women in communities and create safe and non-judgemental dialogues for older women to speak out against abuse. Central to the project is collective organizing and empowerment of older women through peer-to-peer support networks. These safe spaces will offer psychosocial support and serve as platforms for healing, awareness raising, experience sharing, and solidarity building. Concurrently, the project will build the capacity of primary caregivers, who often lack training and information to identify, prevent, and respond to abuse sensitively and effectively. To improve access to justice, the project will support mobile legal aid clinics and grassroots mobile courts, ensuring that legal support reaches older women who cannot travel to distant facilities. Partnerships with local institutions, such as the Court Users Committees (CUCs), will strengthen the capacity of justice actors and create referral pathways tailored to the needs of older survivors. These efforts will be aligned with key advocacy calendar events like the 16 Days of Activism to increase public visibility, mobilize community support, and influence institutional responsiveness. This project envisions a society where older women in Narok and Kitui Counties are safe, heard, and empowered—where their lived realities are acknowledged, and their rights upheld. Through legal empowerment, community education, and intergenerational solidarity, COVAW seeks to disrupt systemic silence and neglect, fostering a more inclusive and just environment for older women.
